value.name: Waffles (with Rhineland Cinnamon Waffle variation)
value.text: A simple waffle batter, plus a Rhineland cinnamon waffle (Rheinische Zimtwaffeln) variation.
ingredients: For Rhineland cinnamon waffles: 125 g butter
For Rhineland cinnamon waffles: 100-125 g sugar
For Rhineland cinnamon waffles: 350 g flour
For Rhineland cinnamon waffles: 100 ml cream
For Rhineland cinnamon waffles: 1-2 teaspoons cinnamon
For Rhineland cinnamon waffles: lemon zest
instructions: Beat together the egg, oil, and milk.
Add the flour, salt, sugar, and baking powder and mix until the batter is slightly lumpy.
Cook in a hot waffle iron until golden.
Rhineland cinnamon waffles: cream the butter, sugar, and eggs until fluffy, then mix in the flour, cream, cinnamon, and lemon zest. Cook in a waffle iron.

value.name: Leek and Bacon Turkey Stuffing
value.text: A savory bread stuffing with leeks, bacon, and fresh herbs - enough for a 12-14 pound turkey.
ingredients: 1 loaf of day-old bread, cubed (about 8 cups)
3 leeks, white and light green parts only, cleaned and sliced
1 cup bacon, diced and cooked until crispy
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Spread the bread cubes on a baking sheet and toast about 10 minutes, until lightly golden. Set aside.
In a large skillet, cook the diced bacon until crispy. Remove the bacon bits and set aside, leaving the bacon fat in the pan.
In the same skillet with the bacon fat, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the onions and leeks and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook another minute until fragrant.
In a large bowl, combine the toasted bread cubes, cooked vegetables, crispy bacon bits, and all the herbs.
Pour the chicken broth and beaten eggs over the mixture, stirring gently to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the stuffing to a greased 9x13-inch baking dish.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes. Then uncover and bake another 15-20 minutes, until the top is golden brown and crispy. Serve hot.

value.name: Tomato Spread (Tomatenaufstrich)
value.text: A vegan tomato spread made from soaked cashews or sunflower seeds blended with sun-dried tomatoes.
instructions: Soak the cashews or sunflower seeds overnight, then drain.
Combine with the remaining ingredients and puree until smooth.

value.name: Quark Pastry Pockets (Teigtaschen)
value.text: Easy quark-dough pockets filled with feta and herbs, brushed with egg and topped with seeds.
ingredients: Filling, e.g. feta, parsley, and olive oil
Sesame, nigella, or poppy seeds, for topping
instructions: Knead the butter, quark, baking powder, flour, and salt into a dough and roll out.
Cut out shapes (e.g. using a large glass) and add the filling (e.g. feta, parsley, and olive oil).
Brush with egg yolk and sprinkle with sesame, nigella, or poppy seeds.
Bake at 160 degrees C (320 degrees F) for 30-40 minutes.

value.name: Spaetzle
value.text: Swabian soft egg noodles, easily turned into cheese Spaetzle (Kaesespaetzle) with cheese and fried onions.
ingredients: For Kaesespaetzle: cheese and fried onions
instructions: Mix the ingredients into a batter.
Press through a Spaetzle grater (or scrape from a board) into boiling salted water.
Skim them out once they float to the surface.
For Kaesespaetzle, toss with cheese and fried onions.

value.name: Bavarian Roast Pork (Schweinebraten)
value.text: A Bavarian pork shoulder roast with crackling, slow-cooked over root vegetables, with a rich beer-and-red-wine gravy.
ingredients: Salt and pepper from the mill
instructions: Do not score the rind yet. Preheat the oven to 130 degrees C (265 degrees F), top and bottom heat. Heat a spoonful of clarified butter in a roasting pan and sear the pork shoulder on all meat sides - but not the rind. Remove the meat.

Pour about half the broth into the roaster (enough to cover the rind) and heat. Lay the pork in rind-side down and braise, covered, in the oven for 1 hour. This softens the rind and guarantees good crackling later.
About 10 minutes before the end, fry the vegetables in clarified butter over high heat until well browned, leaving dark-brown residue in the pan.
Remove the roaster and raise the temperature to 160 degrees C (320 degrees F). Take out the pork and add the roasted vegetables to the roaster.
Now score the rind, not too deep, in diamonds or squares. Salt and pepper the roast, especially the rind. Place the pork on the vegetables rind-side up and braise, covered, another 1.5 hours.

About 10 minutes before the end, in the pan used for the vegetables, caramelize the powdered sugar in a little clarified butter. Add the tomato paste and deglaze with the sweet red wine. Add the rest of the broth (and a splash of beer if you like) and reduce about 10 minutes.
After 1.5 hours, remove the roaster and raise the oven to 220 degrees C (grill with convection). Strain the roasting juices into the pot with the sauce base; discard the vegetables.
Return the pork to the empty roaster rind-side up and roast uncovered about 15 minutes on the lowest rack, relying on top heat, until the crackling is crisp.

Meanwhile, add the bay leaves, crushed garlic, coarsely sliced ginger, and mustard to the sauce. Season with salt and pepper and reduce about 10 minutes. Thicken with a little cornstarch if desired, then strain.
Serve with potato or bread dumplings, which can be prepared during the long roasting time.

value.name: Black Forest Cake (Schwarzwaelder Kirschtorte)
value.text: A chocolate layer cake soaked in kirschwasser, filled with cherries and coffee buttercream, and frosted with whipped cream.
ingredients: 1/2 cup kirschwasser (plus 1 tablespoon for the whipped cream)
2 (14 ounce) cans pitted Bing cherries, drained
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line the bottoms of two 8-inch round pans with parchment circles. Sift together the flour, cocoa, baking soda, and 1 teaspoon salt. Set aside.
Cream the shortening and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the eggs and vanilla. Beat in the flour mixture, alternating with the buttermilk, until combined. Pour into the two pans.

Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 35-40 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely. Remove the paper. Cut each layer in half horizontally, making 4 layers total. Sprinkle the layers with the 1/2 cup kirschwasser.

In a medium bowl, cream the butter until light and fluffy. Add the confectioners' sugar, pinch of salt, and coffee; beat until smooth. If too thick, add a couple teaspoons of cherry juice or milk. Spread the first layer with 1/3 of the filling and top with 1/3 of the cherries. Repeat with the remaining layers.

In a separate bowl, whip the cream to stiff peaks. Beat in 1/2 teaspoon vanilla and 1 tablespoon kirschwasser. Frost the top and sides of the cake. Sprinkle with chocolate curls made with a potato peeler on the semisweet chocolate.

value.name: Rosemary-Apple Roast Pork
value.text: A garlic-and-rosemary marinated pork loin roast served with warm homemade cinnamon applesauce.
ingredients: 4 teaspoons minced fresh rosemary or 1 1/2 teaspoons dried rosemary, crushed
1 boneless pork loin roast (2 to 3 pounds), halved
For the applesauce: 1/4 cup butter, cubed
For the applesauce: 6 medium Golden Delicious apples, peeled and chopped (about 5 cups)
For the applesauce: 1 to 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon
For the applesauce: 2 teaspoons brown sugar
For the applesauce: 1 1/2 teaspoons minced fresh rosemary or 1/2 teaspoon dried rosemary, crushed
instructions: In a large shallow dish, combine the olive oil, salt, garlic powder, rosemary, and pepper. Add the pork and turn to coat. Cover and refrigerate 8 hours or overnight.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Place the pork roast on a rack in a shallow roasting pan, fat side up. Roast until a thermometer reads 145 degrees F, 55-65 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a large skillet, heat the butter over medium heat. Add the apples, cinnamon, brown sugar, rosemary, and salt; cook until the apples are tender, 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the water and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer, uncovered, until the apples are very soft, about 10 minutes. Remove from the heat and mash the apples to the desired consistency.
Remove the roast from the oven and tent with foil. Let stand 10 minutes before slicing. Serve with the warm applesauce.

value.name: Bavarian Pretzel Salad (Brezensalat)
value.text: A Bavarian salad of pan-toasted pretzel pieces with radishes, tomatoes, cucumber, and mountain cheese in a sweet-mustard dressing.
ingredients: 150 g firm mountain cheese (Bergkaese), in one piece
2 large handfuls baby spinach, lamb's lettuce, or mixed leaves
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Cut the pretzels into bite-size pieces and fry in the butter until crispy. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.
Slice the radishes, cut the onion into rings, quarter the tomatoes, and slice the mini cucumbers into rounds. Cube the mountain cheese. Place everything with the baby spinach in a large bowl.
Whisk together the vinegar, mustard, honey, and olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Slice the chives into rolls and add to the dressing.
Add the dressing and the toasted pretzel pieces to the salad and toss gently. Serve.

value.name: Creamy Potato Soup
value.text: A thick, creamy potato soup made lighter with milk and Greek yogurt instead of heavy cream.
ingredients: 1 cup diced white or yellow onion
1.5 pounds potatoes, peeled (if desired) and diced (Yukon gold recommended)
1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt or sour cream
1 teaspoon kosher salt, or more to taste
Optional toppings: thinly sliced green onions or chives, extra cheese, extra bacon, sour cream
instructions: Heat a large stockpot over medium-high heat. Add the diced bacon and cook until crispy, stirring occasionally. Transfer the bacon to a plate with a slotted spoon, reserving about 3 tablespoons of bacon grease in the pot (or substitute butter).

Add the onion and saute 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft. Sprinkle the flour over the onion and stir until combined. Saute another minute to cook the flour. Stir in the chicken stock until combined, then stir in the milk and potatoes. Cook until the mixture reaches a simmer, but is not boiling.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer about 10-15 minutes, or until the potatoes are soft, stirring occasionally so the bottom does not burn.
When the potatoes are soft, stir in the cheddar, Greek yogurt (or sour cream), salt, pepper, and cooked bacon. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve warm, garnished with desired toppings.

value.name: Pizza Dough (Pizzateig)
value.text: A simple thin-crust pizza dough that makes two pizzas.
instructions: Mix the water, yeast, and sugar and let sit about 5 minutes until foamy.
Add the flour and salt and knead into a dough. Let rise until roughly doubled.
Divide in two and shape into two thin-crust pizzas.

value.name: Paella
value.text: A Spanish-style paella with chicken, chorizo, shrimp, mussels, and saffron rice. The cooking steps were reconstructed from the original ingredient list.
ingredients: 4 skinned, boned chicken thighs, cut in half
2 links Spanish chorizo sausage (about 6 1/2 ounces) or turkey kielbasa, cut into 1/2-inch-thick slices
1 (4-ounce) slice prosciutto or 33%-less-sodium ham, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup finely chopped red bell pepper
3 cups uncooked Arborio rice or other short-grain rice
instructions: Combine the water and saffron in a small bowl and let steep. In a saucepan, heat the chicken broth and keep it warm.
Heat the olive oil in a large paella pan or wide skillet over medium-high heat. Season the shrimp and cook briefly until just pink, then remove and set aside.
Add the chicken thighs, chorizo, and prosciutto and cook until browned. Add the onion, bell pepper, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomatoes, paprika, and saffron water. Add the rice and stir to coat.
Pour in the warm broth, bring to a simmer, and cook, mostly undisturbed, until the rice is nearly tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 18-20 minutes.
Nestle in the mussels and peas, arrange the shrimp on top, cover, and cook until the mussels open and the shrimp are cooked through, about 5 minutes more. Discard any unopened mussels.
Drizzle with the lemon juice, rest a few minutes, and serve with lemon wedges.

value.name: Nussecken (Nut Triangles)
value.text: German nut bars: a shortcrust base spread with jam and topped with a nut layer, cut into triangles and dipped in chocolate. Includes two versions.
ingredients: Version 1 topping: 200 g ground coconut flakes, hazelnuts, or almonds
Version 2 topping: vanilla or bitter almond flavoring
instructions: Version 1: Knead the base ingredients into a dough, roll out onto a baking sheet, and prick all over with a fork. Pre-bake at 180 degrees C (355 degrees F) for 20 minutes.
Version 1: Beat the egg whites, stir in the powdered sugar, then fold in the coconut flakes or nuts.
Version 1: Spread the pre-baked base thinly with jam and distribute the meringue-nut mixture on top.
Version 1: Bake again at 150 degrees C (300 degrees F) for 30 minutes. Cut while warm, then decorate with chocolate as desired.
Version 2 (richer): Knead the base ingredients into a dough and roll out.
Version 2: Melt the butter and water in a pot, add the sugar until dissolved, stir in the ground nuts, and add vanilla or bitter almond flavoring.

Version 2: Spread the rolled-out dough with jam (or marzipan), add the nut topping, and bake 35-40 minutes at 180 degrees C (355 degrees F). Cut into triangles when cool and dip the corners in chocolate.

value.name: Creamy Mushroom Sauce
value.text: A rich mushroom sauce with white wine, cream, Parmesan, and fresh thyme.
ingredients: 1 pinch salt and ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the butter and olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until the butter melts. Add the mushrooms and cook until golden brown, 4-5 minutes. Season with garlic, salt, and pepper and cook until the garlic is fragrant, about 1 minute. Pour in the wine and let it sizzle, scraping up the browned bits, until mostly evaporated, about 1 minute.

Stir in the cream and chicken broth, lower the heat to medium, and simmer slowly, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens but does not separate, 2-3 minutes. Stir in the thyme and Parmesan and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.

value.name: Lentil Mushroom Shepherd's Pie
value.text: A vegan shepherd's-pie-style bake with lentils, mushrooms, and herbs under a mashed potato topping.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In a skillet, heat the olive oil and saute the onion, garlic, carrot, and celery until soft and fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and cooked lentils along with the soy sauce, tomato paste, thyme, and rosemary. Stir together for a few minutes.
Pour in the vegetable broth and let simmer about 10 minutes so the flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the lentil mixture to a baking dish. Mash the potatoes with the plant-based milk and a little salt, then spread over the top.
Bake about 20-25 minutes, until the topping is golden. Let rest a few minutes before serving.

value.name: Lemon Custard
value.text: A simple set lemon cream custard, optionally served in hollowed-out lemon rinds.
instructions: Simmer the cream and sugar together. Add the vanilla, then add the lemon juice toward the end.
Pour into a bowl or hollowed-out lemon rinds and let set in the fridge.

value.name: Oven Potato Wedges (Kartoffelspalten)
value.text: Crispy seasoned oven-baked potato wedges with paprika, oregano, and polenta for crunch.
instructions: Mix the oil, paprika, oregano, salt, pepper, and polenta.
Cut the potatoes into wedges and toss them in the mixture.
Preheat the oven to 230 degrees C (445 degrees F), heating the baking sheet along with it.
Spread the wedges on parchment paper and bake on the middle rack for 25-30 minutes.

value.name: German Potato Salad (Kartoffelsalat)
value.text: A cool German-style potato salad with a tangy mustard-pickle vinaigrette - best made ahead and left to soak overnight.
instructions: Boil the potatoes with 1 tablespoon salt (and 1 tablespoon caraway, if using) until cooked but still fairly firm. Drain, rinse, let cool slightly, and peel while lukewarm.

In a large sealable jar, combine the mustard, sugar, pickle juice, vinegar, oil, a little salt, plenty of pepper, and the finely chopped onion (and garlic if using). Shake vigorously to make a vinaigrette emulsion.
Peel and finely chop the apple if using; slice the pickles; slice the lukewarm potatoes.
Layer the potato slices, pickles, and apple in a large bowl, spooning some vinaigrette and a little salt and pepper between the layers.

There should be slightly too much marinade in the salad. Let it soak at least 3-4 hours, ideally overnight - the potatoes absorb the marinade and stay juicy without getting mushy. Mix well before serving.
Garnish with green onions or chives.

value.name: Potato Dumplings (Kartoffelknoedel)
value.text: Bavarian-style potato dumplings made from floury potatoes and potato starch - a classic side for roasts.
ingredients: 1.5 kg floury potatoes, boiled the day before
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until done.
When slightly cooled, peel them and press through a potato ricer.

Once the potatoes are only lukewarm, add the melted butter, egg, nutmeg, and potato starch. On a surface dusted with potato starch, knead carefully into a smooth dough. Add a little more starch if needed, but not too much or the dumplings won't be light. Chill the dough for 1 day.
The next day, roll the dumplings to the desired size and dust lightly with potato starch so they don't stick. (If not cooking immediately, keep them chilled.)
Bring a large pot of salted water to a simmer, reduce the temperature (the dumplings must not boil), and slide the dumplings in to cook gently. Don't cook too many at once.
When the dumplings float to the surface (often after just 8-10 minutes), turn off the heat, wait 1 minute, then drain.

value.name: Jaegerschnitzel (Schnitzel with Mushroom Sauce)
value.text: Pan-fried schnitzel in a creamy mushroom sauce with porcini and creme fraiche.
ingredients: 100 ml dry white wine or vegetable broth
instructions: Season the schnitzel with salt and pepper. Heat the clarified butter in a saute pan and fry the schnitzel about 2 minutes per side. Remove and keep warm, covered.
For the sauce, soak the dried porcini in lukewarm water. Clean the fresh mushrooms, pat dry, and slice thinly. Fry them over high heat about 3 minutes, stirring.
Drain and squeeze out the soaked porcini, chop finely, and fry together with the shallots about 1 minute. Dust with the flour.
Add the white wine and deglaze with the creme fraiche. Cover and simmer over low heat about 5 minutes.
Return the schnitzel to the sauce and let them sit in it about 3 minutes more. Serve the schnitzel with the mushroom sauce.

value.name: Irish Lamb Stew
value.text: A hearty Guinness-style lamb stew with bacon, root vegetables, and herbs.
ingredients: 6 pounds boneless lamb shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 large onions, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Transfer with a slotted spoon to a paper-towel-lined plate to drain. Reserve the bacon fat in the skillet.

Place lamb, flour, salt, and pepper in a large bowl and toss to coat evenly. Brown the lamb in the bacon fat over medium-high heat. Transfer the browned meat into a stockpot, leaving 1/4 cup of fat in the skillet.

Cook the onion and garlic in the reserved fat over medium heat until the onion is golden. Deglaze the skillet with water, then pour the onion mixture into the stockpot. Add the bacon, beef stock, and sugar. Cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add the carrots, potatoes, onions, wine, thyme, and bay leaves. Reduce the heat and simmer, covered, until the vegetables are tender, about 20 minutes.

value.name: Yeast Cake with Cinnamon Topping (Hefekuchen)
value.text: A classic German sweet yeast dough for a sheet cake, plus a cinnamon-sugar topping variation (Zimtkuchen).
ingredients: For the cinnamon topping: melted butter
instructions: Stir the yeast smooth in a little lukewarm milk. Put the flour in a bowl, make a well, and stir the yeast mixture into a small pre-dough in the center (about the thickness of a thick pancake batter).
Cover and let the pre-dough rise in a warm place.

Add the lukewarm melted butter and the remaining ingredients to the pre-dough. Knead vigorously, adding enough lukewarm milk until the dough is smooth, supple, and pulls away from the bowl - knead until it forms bubbles.
Let rise again in a warm place until doubled in size.
Roll out the dough and place on a well-greased baking sheet.

For Zimtkuchen: spread the dough about 2 cm thick in a greased pan and let rise another 15 minutes. Just before baking, brush with melted butter, sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon, and bake at moderate heat (170-180 degrees C / 340-355 degrees F) for 30 minutes.

value.name: Mulled Wine Spice (Gluehweingewuerz)
value.text: Spice blends for making mulled wine (Gluehwein), with separate mixes for red and white wine, each per 1 liter.
ingredients: For red wine (per 1 L): 1 organic orange, peel or slices
For red wine: 2 cinnamon sticks (or 1 teaspoon ground)
For red wine: 5 cloves (or 1 teaspoon ground)
For red wine: 4 cardamom pods (or 1 teaspoon ground)
For red wine: 3 whole star anise
For red wine: 3 tablespoons brown rock sugar (or white sugar)
For white wine (per 1 L): 1 organic orange, peel or slices
For white wine: 1 organic lemon, peel
For white wine: 1 knife-tip ginger powder
For white wine: 1 vanilla pod (or 1 sachet vanilla sugar)
instructions: Mix together the ingredients for either the red or white mulled wine blend.
To make a larger batch to store, scale up the amounts and mix well. Fill into light-proof tins and use within about 2 months (jars work too, but store them in the dark).
To grind cardamom or star anise fresh, use a spice or coffee grinder, or a mortar (note the spices won't dissolve as finely).
It's best to use ground spices for the fine ingredients and leave coarse ones - cinnamon stick, vanilla pod, star anise - whole, removing them before serving.

value.name: Germknoedel (Sweet Yeast Dumplings)
value.text: Austrian-style steamed sweet yeast dumplings served with poppy-seed butter and vanilla sauce.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons freshly ground poppy seeds (10 g)
instructions: Sift the flour into a bowl and make a well in the center.
Pour 125 ml lukewarm milk into the well, crumble in the yeast, and mix with the honey. Stir, then let rise in a warm place 10-15 minutes.
Add a little salt and the egg to the dough. Beat with a wooden spoon until the dough forms bubbles.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir the vanilla pudding powder with a little milk. Bring the remaining milk to a boil, stir in the pudding powder, boil briefly, sweeten with the cane sugar, and let cool.
Knead the dough briefly and divide into four portions. Shape into four dumplings and let rise, covered, another 15 minutes.
Gently poach the dumplings in simmering water until done.
Melt the butter in a pan, add the poppy seeds, and saute. Deglaze with the orange juice and let the poppy seeds swell 10 minutes.
Lift the dumplings out with a slotted spoon, arrange on plates, and coat with the poppy-seed butter. Serve the vanilla sauce on the side.

value.name: Vegetable Quiche (Gemuesequiche)
value.text: A savory quiche with a buttery shortcrust base and a creamy egg-and-vegetable filling.
instructions: Knead the flour, butter, salt, and 1 egg into a dough. Roll out and line a tart pan, then add the steamed vegetables.
Mix the cream, sour cream, 2 eggs, salt, pepper, and nutmeg, and pour over the vegetables.
Sprinkle with cheese and bake at 180 degrees C (355 degrees F) for 30 minutes.

value.name: Flammkuchen (Alsatian Tarte Flambee)
value.text: A thin, crispy Alsatian flatbread topped with creme fraiche, onions, and bacon.
instructions: Make a kneaded dough from the flour, oil, water, and salt; it should not feel sticky.
Slice the onions thinly; cut the bacon into thin, narrow strips.
Roll the dough out very thin and spread with creme double (or creme fraiche blended with a little sweet cream). Distribute the onions and bacon on top.
Bake in a preheated oven at the highest setting about 15-20 minutes, until the base is crisp.

value.name: Cheese Buns
value.text: Soft enriched rolls rolled with grated cheddar, plus variations for plain dinner rolls.
ingredients: 2 cups bread flour (all-purpose can be substituted)
1/4 cup butter, margarine, or shortening, softened
1 egg yolk plus water to measure 3/4 cup
instructions: Mix and knead the dough. Place in a warm spot about an hour, covered with a barely damp towel, and let rise.
Punch the dough down and let it rise again for half an hour.
On a floured surface, roll the dough into a large rectangle. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Sprinkle the dough with grated cheese and roll it into a cylinder.
Slice the cylinder into buns just over an inch thick.
Place buns on a greased pan, cover with a damp towel, and let rise in a warm spot about 1 hour.
Brush with beaten egg yolk and bake at 375 degrees F for 8-10 minutes.
Bow Knots variation: roll the dough into 12 ropes about 8 inches long, tie each into a knot, place on a greased baking sheet, then let rise and bake as directed.
Clover Leaf Rolls variation: shape the dough into 36 balls, place 3 in each greased muffin cup, let rise, brush with melted butter, and bake as directed.

Parker House Rolls variation: roll the dough into a 12-inch round, cut 12 rolls with a 2-inch cutter, spread each with 1/4 teaspoon softened butter, fold in half and press lightly, then let rise and bake as directed.

value.name: Carrot 'Salmon' (Vegan Carrot Lox)
value.text: Marinated carrot ribbons that mimic smoked salmon - great on bread like lox or with rice for sushi.
ingredients: 500-600 g carrots, as thick as possible
7-10 drops liquid smoke (or smoked salt or smoked paprika)
Optional: dill and lemon juice (for a lox-on-bread style)
Optional: 1 sheet dried nori/gim seaweed (for a rice/sushi style)
instructions: Peel the carrots. Using the peeler, shave them into even ribbons; start on one side until you have a flat surface, then lay the carrot on it for stability.
Blanch the carrot ribbons in boiling water 3-5 minutes depending on thickness - they should stay al dente, not fall apart.
Meanwhile, stir together the marinade of salt, sugar, vinegar, caper brine, and liquid smoke in a bowl or sealable container.
If using, add dill (for a Scandinavian gravlax flavor) and/or nori (for an East Asian flavor) to the marinade.
Drain the carrots and, while still warm, add them to the marinade. Stir gently and let marinate at least 30 minutes, ideally longer.
Stored sealed in the fridge it keeps about a week, getting stronger in flavor over time.

value.name: Candied Almonds (Gebrannte Mandeln)
value.text: German fairground-style candied almonds coated in spiced caramel - a classic Christmas-market treat.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon gingerbread spice (Lebkuchengewuerz: cinnamon, clove, allspice, nutmeg, cardamom, ginger, anise)
200 g whole almonds with skin (or cashews, walnuts, or pecans)
instructions: In a large pan, bring the sugar, water, salt, and gingerbread spice to a boil over high heat, stirring.
Add the almonds and stir constantly from now on.
Simmer until the water slowly evaporates, about 5-10 minutes. The sugar will caramelize, then turn dusty and grainy around the almonds. Reduce to medium heat.
Keep stirring and raise the heat again. Add 2-3 tablespoons of water; the caramel will turn liquid and smooth and coat the almonds in a glossy layer. Watch that the caramel doesn't get too dark.
Spread the candied almonds on parchment paper, separate them, and let cool. Stored in a sealed tin they keep up to four weeks.

value.name: No-Knead Dutch Oven Bread (Brot im Topf)
value.text: An easy, quick, and tasty no-knead bread baked in a covered pot.
instructions: Stir all ingredients together and let rise for 3 hours.
Line a pot with parchment paper and add the dough. Dust the dough with flour.
Bake covered at 250 degrees C (480 degrees F) with top and bottom heat for 30 minutes.
Optionally remove the parchment and bake another 30 minutes uncovered.

value.name: German Lye Pretzels (Brezeln)
value.text: Soft German lye pretzels (Laugenbrezeln) with a chewy interior and deep brown crust.
ingredients: 250 g milk, oat, or soy milk - or 125 ml beer (lager, wheat, or pilsner) plus 125 ml water
15 g fresh yeast (or 8 g dry yeast); optionally 150 g sourdough starter
For the lye bath: 2 liters water
For the lye bath: 40 g baking soda
For the lye bath: 15 g salt
instructions: Warm the milk to room temperature or slightly warmer, stir in the yeast and sugar, and let sit about 5 minutes.
Combine all dough ingredients and knead into a dough for about 10 minutes.
Either let rise about 1 hour until roughly doubled, or let rise slowly in the fridge at least 8 hours (ideally 24-36) for more flavor.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces. Flatten each, fold into a roll, and stretch into a long rope that is thinner at the ends. Shape into a pretzel with the classic knot.
Bring the baking-soda bath to a boil and dip each pretzel about 1 minute, then place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Cut a shallow slit along the thick part of each pretzel and sprinkle with coarse salt and/or herbs.
Preheat the oven to 220 degrees C (430 degrees F) and bake for 20 minutes.

value.name: Berry Liqueur (Beerenlikoer)
value.text: A homemade berry liqueur (also called Holunderfeuer) made by steeping berries with rock sugar and spirits.
ingredients: 200 g berries (e.g. a mix of elderberries and sloes)
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a clean bottle.
Let steep on a windowsill for 2 months, shaking occasionally.
Strain and enjoy. The soaked berries are also tasty.

value.name: Bacon Cheddar Gnocchi Soup
value.text: A creamy potato gnocchi soup with crispy bacon, sharp cheddar, and thyme.
instructions: In a large pot, cook the chopped bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove the bacon and set aside, leaving the bacon fat in the pot.
Add butter to the pot, followed by the diced onion and minced garlic. Saute until the onion becomes translucent.
Stir in the flour and cook about 2 minutes to make a roux. Slowly whisk in the chicken broth and half-and-half, ensuring there are no lumps.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Add the potato gnocchi and cook about 5 minutes, until they float to the surface.
Stir in the shredded cheddar, cooked bacon, thyme, salt, and pepper to taste.
Simmer another 5 minutes, allowing the soup to thicken.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

value.name: Babylonian Tuh'u (Lamb and Beet Stew)
value.text: A modern reconstruction of an ancient Babylonian lamb and beet stew from the Yale Babylonian tablets (c. 1740 BC).
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) leg of lamb, cut into bite-size pieces
12 oz (350 ml) beer (a sour beer or German Weissbier recommended; any non-hoppy beer works)
Egyptian-style leek, for garnish (substitute for suhutinnu)
instructions: Add the oil or fat to a large pot over high heat. Sear the lamb for several minutes until lightly browned.

Add the onions and cook 5 minutes, then add the beets and cook 5 minutes more. Add the salt, beer, water, arugula, cilantro, shallot, cumin, and coriander and bring to a boil. Mash the garlic into a paste, mix with the leek, and add to the pot.
Lower the heat to medium and simmer about 1 hour, until the beets and meat are cooked to your liking.
Serve in bowls sprinkled with coriander seeds. Garnish with fresh cilantro and leek.

value.name: Apple Roses
value.text: Puff pastry and thinly sliced apple 'roses' baked in a muffin tin and dusted with powdered sugar.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon flour, for dusting the counter
instructions: Thaw the puff pastry if you haven't already; it takes about 20-30 minutes.
Thinly slice the apples, place in a bowl with the lemon juice and a little water, and microwave about 3 minutes to soften slightly (or simmer the slices in a small pan on the stove).
In a bowl, combine 3 tablespoons apricot preserve with 2 tablespoons water and microwave about 1 minute so it spreads easily.
Roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface and cut into strips. Spread the preserve over the dough.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Drain the apples.
Arrange overlapping apple slices along the top half of each dough strip. Sprinkle with cinnamon if desired.
Fold the bottom half of the dough up over the apples.
Carefully roll up each strip, seal the edge, and place in a silicone muffin cup (grease the cups if not using silicone).

Repeat for all 6 roses. Bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for about 40-45 minutes, until fully cooked through. If the apples look done after 30 minutes, move the pan to a lower rack and bake 10-15 minutes more so the pastry cooks through.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve.
